final_answer:
The provided evidence does not contain enough information to determine the highest detection rate achieved by any single indicator across all detection tiers.

While the text mentions specific detection rates for certain indicators in specific contexts, it lacks a comprehensive list of all indicators tested across all tiers with their corresponding maximum rates. The available data points are:
- **JA4 fingerprints**: Achieved 100% detection in one context (page 1) [c1], but the evidence does not explicitly state this was the highest rate across *all* tiers or if it applies to a broader set of indicators.
- **Beacon Detection (Clustering)**: Detected 2 out of 4 frameworks (50%) [c1, c3].
- **Traffic Patterns**: Mentioned as "most viable" but no specific percentage is given for its highest rate [c1].
- **Reputation-based detection**: Failed to identify any C2 channels (0% detection) [c1, c4].

The evidence notes that JA4 fingerprints showed a unique signature for each framework [c3], implying high individual accuracy, but it does not explicitly compare this against other indicators across the full scope of "all detection tiers" to confirm 100% is the absolute highest rate globally within the study. Without a complete dataset of every indicator's performance across every tier, the exact maximum cannot be definitively identified from the text alone.

citations.title: Network Artifacts of Trusted Service Abuse (page 1)
citations.snippet: sing 51 packet captures (3 baselines, 6 automated browser tests and 6 framework tests per service). Across four detection tiers, Reputation-based detection failed to identify any C2 channels; Beacon Detection was marginally viable when using clustering (2/4); Traffic Metadata was partially viable, with mixed results other than JA4 fingerprints (100% detection); and Traffic Patterns proved most viable, with both TLS session resumption near-zero (vs 22%+ for browser) and a 2.6x upload/download ratio gap (1.41 vs 0.55 means). Structural and behavioral indicators, such as TLS session resumption and JA4 fingerprinting, outperform reputation in detecting trusted service abuse.

citations.title: Network Artifacts of Trusted Service Abuse (page 23)
citations.snippet: Network Artifacts of Trusted Service Abuse 23 Nicholas Vaniscak, vaniscak.nicholas@gmail.com 4. Recommendations and Implications 4.1. Summary of Findings Results meet expectations: Domain & IP Reputation is not a viable detection mechanism and provides no reliable indications of Command-and-Control Frameworks. As anticipated from the short observation windows, beacon detection was only partially viable; the simplest method produced no indications, and while clustering appears plausible, it detected only half of the tested frameworks. With a solid network baseline, a difficult ask, metadata-driven indications become useful: each framework exhibited a unique JA4 signature clearly...
